summary:
Scope: how a timer-driven capture of new and grown Claude transcripts was built on the passive path (coord 0.114 engine, Host 0.9.0 receiver), from the cited sources. Process knowledge from one build, not a contract; the constants live in the cited code and may change.

Why not a fresh second association or a new principal: the capture state keeps compact retired-source entries and a bounded set of recently retired identities (SkillTelemetryAdapter). A transcript that is resumed after it was captured is recognised from those entries and either resumed or suppressed. A fresh state has none, so it would re-emit identities already stored, and the receiver refuses a repeated identity as a conflict and quarantines the batch. Reusing the state also needs no receiver change, no second credential copy and no second drain unit.

Selection arithmetic: the state keeps at most 8 active source cursors (one was a Codex source that stays active), an active Claude source holds its newest 24 responses, and the total is capped at 256, so a selection of at most 7 files stays under both. A source retires only when a pass has read it to a line-boundary end and the file has been unmodified for 900 s, and only if it is scanned in that pass. A pass that produces no ready file means the selection is read to its end; a file that was still being written then needs one more scan after the quiet period to release its slot. Files that never quiet down keep their slots; others wait for a free slot, oldest modification first.

Operating rules that held: baseline every existing file as seen so the start is forward-only; select only files that are new, grown or due for the post-quiet scan; keep unfinished files selected until exhausted; count receipts from the receiver and outcome files, with no private ledger, since the unattended drain may apply the timer's own batch; wait for the drain service to be idle and its next tick to be more than about 55 s away; bound each run (a few capture and drain rounds); reaching a daily receipt cap skips quietly; every earlier stop (rejected receipt, control drift, retained over 235, a gap name, a non-zero exit, a forbidden string in a batch) writes a marker that disables later runs until a person clears it. Check a first supervised run for the receipt, the fact count and the absence of duplicate identities before enabling the timer.
title: Continuous Claude capture reuses the existing capture state: retired cursors prevent duplicate identities; the 8-cursor and 256-identity limits cap it
